deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to the manuscript on Gaussian quadrature behind Gauss's 'Methodus nova integralium valores per approximationem inveniendi' (presented 1814, published 1816). The previous page builds the node polynomial T (Legendre-type) and expresses the weights through U.

(1) Six-point rule. The nodes are the roots of 0 = t^6 - (15/11)t^4 + (5/11)t^2 - 5/231. This is the monic Legendre polynomial P_6, since 16 P_6(t) = 231t^6 - 315t^4 + 105t^2 - 5. Its roots are ±a, ±b, ±c. Gauss tabulates:
- the squares aa = 0.05693911596, bb = 0.43719735273, cc = 0.86949939497;
- their Briggsian logarithms in the -10 convention (8.75541072, 9.64067302, 9.93926928);
- the roots a = 0.2386192, b = 0.6612094, c = 0.9324696;
- the fourth powers a^4 = 0.00324206293, b^4 = 0.19114196244, c^4 = 0.75602919777 (input for the polynomial weight formula of the previous page);
- the Christoffel weights on [-1,1], A_i = 2/((1 - t_i^2) P_6'(t_i)^2): 0.467913934572, 0.360761573048, 0.171324492379.
These weights sum to 1 per symmetric pair, so 2 in total.

(2) Worked example (Beispiel einer Anwendung): I = ∫ dx/log x from 100000 to 200000, i.e. li(2·10^5) - li(10^5).
- Substitution (mine, implicit on the page): x = 100000(1+u) with u in [0,1], so I = 100000 ∫_0^1 du/ln x.
- Nodes on [0,1]: u_i = (1+t_i)/2.
- Columns of each table: column 1 is log10 x_i; column 2 is log10(log10 x_i), a logarithm used for the division; column 3 is the term 100000 · (A_i/2) / (ln10 · log10 x_i).
- Example: the 7-point middle node is x = 150000, log10 = 5.1760912591, with weight 0.2089796. This gives 20897.96/(2.302585·5.17609) = 1753.4212 ✓.

Sums of the terms:
| Points | Sum |
|---|---|
| 7 | 8406.2431211 |
| 6 | 8406.2431207 |
| 5 | 8406.2431172 |
| 4 | 8406.2429694 |
| 3 | 8406.2367758 |
| 2 | 8405.9545986 |
| 1 (midpoint) | 8390.3946079 |

(3) 'Fehler': the errors of the n-point results, taking the 7-point value as exact:
- I = 15.8485132
- II = 0.2885225
- III = 0.0063453
- IV = 0.0001517
- V = 0.0000039
- VI = 0.0000001
The error falls by a factor of about 40–55 per added node, showing the rapid convergence of the method.
errors: 4-point table: the second-column values (log log x) for rows 2–4 are written in the wrong order. 0.7178962447 belongs to 5.2227140063, 0.7231012892 to 5.2856851384, and 0.7095968088 to 5.1238547360. Gauss's bracket/arrow on the page marks this reordering; the third-column terms are computed correctly.
5-point: the first term was first written as 972.4277629 (wrongly, by analogy with the symmetric last term) and corrected to 1024.8794451; the corrected value is right.

6-point: the six terms as transcribed (last term 702.7805709) add to 8406.2431215, not the stated 8406.2431207. The last digits of 702.78057.. are overwritten in the manuscript; 702.7805701 would give the stated sum.

Error VI: taking the 7-point value 8406.2431211 as reference, as for errors I–V, the 6-point error is 0.0000004, not 0.0000001. Gauss may have used a slightly different reference value or a different 6-point sum; this is a minor last-digit inconsistency.
Second column of 6-point row 1: 0.70022087[38] was corrected to ...33 (superscript 3); log10(5.0144219263) = 0.7002208733..., so the correction is right.

results.what: Nodes of the 6-point rule as roots of the monic Legendre polynomial t^6 - 15/11 t^4 + 5/11 t^2 - 5/231, with roots, squares, fourth powers and weights to 10–11 places
results.usually_credited_to: C. F. Gauss, Methodus nova integralium valores per approximationem inveniendi (1814/1816); tables published there

results.what: Numerical comparison of 1- to 7-point Gaussian quadrature on ∫dx/log x from 10^5 to 2·10^5 (≈8406.24312), with error table
results.modern_name: Gauss–Legendre quadrature applied to the logarithmic integral li(x) difference
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss 1814; this same example is the worked example in the published Methodus nova

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft computation for the published 1814 paper on Gaussian quadrature, including its own worked example ∫dx/log x from 100000 to 200000. The material is fully known as Gauss's; only minor arithmetic corrections are visible.

checkable.asserts: The equation is the monic Legendre polynomial P_6 (difference is 0).

checkable.sympy: [N(r,12) for r in nroots(t**6 - Rational(15,11)*t**4 + Rational(5,11)*t**2 - Rational(5,231), n=15)]

Equation sign: the constant term is −5/231 (the image shows an overwritten bar), consistent with P_6.
